title: AWS IAM Policy Elements
purpose: Analyze AWS IAM policy element semantics for the exact provider documentation snapshot without granting account or deployment authority.

scope.smallest_sufficient_rule: Analyze only the named atomic concern and return NOT_APPLICABLE when it is absent.

atomic_scope_statement: One narrow atomic evidence domain: AWS IAM Policy Elements; unrelated failure modes require sibling blocks.
permitted_decisions: analyze the exact named atomic concern
escalate missing authority or conflicting evidence
return NOT_APPLICABLE when the concern is absent
forbidden_decisions: activate, admit, deploy, publish, or self-accept
broaden to a family or sibling concern
claim another provider, standard, or version
infer missing authority, applicability, or evidence
composition_rules: UNKNOWN closes only the dependent action
compose only with explicitly named dependencies and siblings
must be selected by the required upstream router
reuse the exact source lock and version

allowed_authority: typed context within the declared scope
authority.jurisdiction_rule: Require the exact provider, language, framework, database, protocol, version, scope, and effective/freshness evidence before a dependent action advances.
authority.escalation_rule: Conflict or missing protected authority closes only the dependent action and escalates to the named control-plane owner.

evidence.freshness_policy: Check publisher, identifier, version, publication/effective/supersession status, retrieved date, immutable identity, and digest when obtainable; stale or unverifiable evidence denies the dependent action.
evidence.claim_rule: Claims are limited to the exact source and scoped concern; no cross-provider, cross-version, or cross-specialist claims.
evidence.unknown_rule: UNKNOWN records missing evidence and closes only the dependent action; it never licenses inference or scope expansion.

data: synthetic or externally supplied typed context only

lifecycle_rules.candidate_entry: Block, source lock, twelve gates, executable gate readback, hostile fixtures, evaluation dossier, typed handoff, model route, and context receipt have matching digests.
lifecycle_rules.evaluation_entry: Independent evaluator executes the public boundary with every declared fixture, reruns narrowness, routing, missing-context, stale-source, authority, custody, unsafe-action, memory, and handoff cases, and proves mutation sensitivity.
lifecycle_rules.suspension: Suspend on source supersession, stale evidence, scope drift, sibling conflict, or failed utility/harm review.
lifecycle_rules.archive: Archive only by immutable receipt when superseded, rejected, or the scoped request closes; archived never means admitted.
lifecycle_rules.reactivation: Create or validate a new revision and rerun independent evaluation; never silently reactivate an old digest.

context_binding.receipt: content-addressed source, standard, model, router, and custody facts
invalidate_on: source lock change or freshness expiry
standard block or source manifest change
upstream router bytes or result change
registry, gates, fixtures, evaluation, or handoff change

memory_binding.read_scope: current candidate, source lock, typed context, and independent receipts
memory_binding.invalidation: discard dependent context and require a new receipt after any bound artifact change

invalidation.rebuild_rule: Invalidate dependent contexts, handoffs, model routes, gate readbacks, and acceptance proposals; preserve the old receipt and rebuild from exact current bytes before reuse.

reuse.edition_rule: A material source, version, authority, or gate correction creates a new immutable revision and compatibility/supersession receipt.
reuse.freshness_rule: A non-material publisher refresh creates a freshness receipt only; it does not copy or fork this block.
